cve_summary: The sctp_sf_do_5_2_4_dupcook function in net/sctp/sm_statefuns.c in the SCTP implementation in the Linux kernel before 3.8.5 does not properly handle associations during the processing of a duplicate COOKIE ECHO chunk, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted SCTP traffic.
commit_message:
sctp: Use correct sideffect command in duplicate cookie handling

When SCTP is done processing a duplicate cookie chunk, it tries
to delete a newly created association.  For that, it has to set
the right association for the side-effect processing to work.
However, when it uses the SCTP_CMD_NEW_ASOC command, that performs
more work then really needed (like hashing the associationa and
assigning it an id) and there is no point to do that only to
delete the association as a next step.  In fact, it also creates
an impossible condition where an association may be found by
the getsockopt() call, and that association is empty.  This
causes a crash in some sctp getsockopts.

The solution is rather simple.  We simply use SCTP_CMD_SET_ASOC
command that doesn't have all the overhead and does exactly
what we need.

Reported-by: Karl Heiss <kheiss@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Karl Heiss <kheiss@gmail.com>
CC: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Signed-off-by: Vlad Yasevich <vyasevich@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
docstring:
/**
 * Summary: Handles the processing of a duplicate COOKIE ECHO chunk in SCTP.
 * 
 * Parameters:
 * net (struct net *): The network context for the operation.
 * ep (const struct sctp_endpoint *): The SCTP endpoint associated with the operation.
 * asoc (const struct sctp_association *): The current SCTP association.
 * type (sctp_subtype_t): The subtype of the SCTP event.
 * arg (void *): A pointer to the SCTP chunk being processed.
 * commands (sctp_cmd_seq_t *): A sequence of commands to be executed.
 * 
 * Returns: sctp_disposition_t - The disposition of the chunk processing, indicating success, failure, or memory error.
 * 
 * Logic: The function first validates the length of the chunk. It then decodes the chunk and attempts to unpack the state cookie. Depending on the outcome, it may handle various error cases or compare verification tags to determine the appropriate action (restart association, handle collisions, or discard the packet). Finally, it updates the command sequence and returns the result of the processing.
 */
